name: אָחָז
summary: Above all Ahaz son of Jotham, king of Judah, who “did not do what was right in the eyes of Yahweh”, made his son pass through the fire, and sent to Tiglath-pileser for help against Rezin and Pekah, copying the altar he saw at Damascus (2Ki 16:2–4, 7–16; 2Ch 28:1–4, 16–25). To him Isaiah was sent with the sign of the virgin's son Immanuel, after Ahaz had refused to ask a sign (Isa 7:1–14), which Matthew quotes of Jesus' birth (Mat 1:23); and the shadow went back ten steps on “the steps of Ahaz” for his son Hezekiah (2Ki 20:11; Isa 38:8). He is in the genealogy of Jesus (Mat 1:9, Ἀχάζ). The name is also borne by a Benjamite of Saul's line, son of Micah (1Ch 8:35–36; 9:41–42). The name is the qal perfect of אָחַז, “he has taken hold”; scripture does not explain it, and does not say who is the subject.

evidence.note: “Ahaz son of Jotham king of Judah began to reign.”
“He did not do what was right in the eyes of Yahweh his God … he even made his son pass through the fire.”
“I am your servant and your son; come up and save me”, to the king of Assyria.
“In the days of Ahaz son of Jotham … Rezin and Pekah went up to Jerusalem to war against it.”
“I will not ask, and I will not test Yahweh.”
“The virgin shall conceive and bear a son and call his name Immanuel”, the sign given to the house of David in Ahaz's day.
The shadow went back ten steps on the steps of Ahaz.
“In the time of his distress he trespassed yet more against Yahweh, this King Ahaz.”
“Jotham begot Ahaz (Ἀχάζ), and Ahaz begot Hezekiah”; the Peshitta writes אחז.
“The sons of Micah: Pithon, Melech, Tarea and Ahaz; and Ahaz begot Jehoaddah.”

note: Takes a.cl.ab (41 tokens). The reading “he has taken hold” takes the name as the qal perfect, perhaps shortened from a name with Yahweh as subject, as יְהוֹאָחָז (names/jehoahaz.json); Tiglath-pileser's annals are said to call him Ia-ú-ḫa-zi (Jehoahaz), not followed to an edition. TIPNR keys the Benjamite as Ahaz@1Ch.8.35.
